::: {.home-lead}
Hello! I'm Victor, a data scientist at Sonoma Biotherapeutics. I help develop T-cell-based therapies for autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis. My favorite part of the job is working with brilliant colleagues on new drugs that could improve patients' lives.

::: {.home-copy}
I first encountered bioinformatics in 2016 as a first-year graduate student in UBC's Genome Sciences and Technology program. My undergrad was in Cell and Molecular Biology (Honours thesis: CRISPR x Yeast), so I was coming in pretty green to computation and statistics. I feel fortunate to have spent the next five years in an incredibly supportive environment, learning about bioinformatics, genomics, and machine learning. My PhD thesis applied machine learning and cellular epigenetics to study placental development.

I graduated with my PhD in 2022, which we can now look back on as a significantly brighter time in biotech's recent history, and then found myself at Jeff Bluestone's Treg company Sonoma, where I still work today. There I worked alongside incredibly talented and kind colleagues on developing a very exciting novel therapy.
:::

::: {.home-copy}
<h2>I'm a good thinker</h2>

I think I've always been good at thinking things through. I'm the type of person to spend a lot of time planning before taking action. As a scientist, and specifically one that lives in data, I bring value in interpreting what data means, what conclusions can be drawn, what it means for the next steps, and what limitations are crucial to keep in mind.
:::
::::

:::: {.home-row .home-strength}
<div class="home-number" aria-hidden="true">2</div>

::: {.home-copy}
<h2>I'm good at presenting data</h2>

I don't know why, but there is something innate in me that whenever I see a graph, my mind impulsively lists off criticisms, even small ones: *why is the font size so small? The axis labels are not informative. Pie charts need to die.* I probably spend too much time on my graphics. But the occasional praise is often worth it. I've even won some contests for my visualizations. <!--- link to plotnine / table contest winnings --->
:::
::::

:::: {.home-row .home-strength}
<div class="home-number" aria-hidden="true">3</div>

::: {.home-copy}
<h2>I respect data integrity</h2>

I'm not sure if this one is going to be that relevant anymore. But ever since undergrad, I've been taught that good science is reproducible. When I became a data scientist, I applied that to everything involving data: documentation, reproducible practices (e.g., Git, Quarto/R Markdown), and these days, "big boy" data engineering tools like dbt, Prefect, GitHub Actions, and CI/CD.
:::
